processing: As with other Yunnan raw pu-erh, the leaf is typically wilted, wok-fired, rolled and sun-dried into mao cha, then sold loose or steamed and pressed; no ripe-style pile fermentation.
harvest_season: Spring is the prized picking, as is usual for Mengku raw pu-erh; little is documented about the season here beyond that.
appearance_dry: Typical of Mengku large-leaf raw tea: long, thick dark strands with some tip.
appearance_liquor: Typically clear golden yellow when young.
appearance_wet: Thick large leaves in olive green, as with other Mengku raw teas.
taste_profile: Little is documented about Banggai's own taste; Mengku raw tea in general is sweet, fragrant and vigorous.

brewing.notes: General Mengku raw settings, since nothing specific to Banggai is recorded.

vintage_note: Sold by harvest year like other sheng: mostly as spring tea of a stated year, either as loose mao cha or pressed cakes. Young cakes of one to three years are the usual purchase, and those who store it age it for a decade or more. Ask for the year and the tree age, since old-tree and plantation leaf are priced far apart.
description:
Banggai is a village committee on Mengku's western half-mountain, one Lahu and four Han villages whose living is mainly tea. It is counted among the Mengku Eighteen Villages, and it has served as a seed source for neighbouring gardens.

Its leaf is regarded locally as authentic Mengku large-leaf, and its processing has a good reputation among those who have visited. Beyond that, the method is the usual raw pu-erh one of the area.

No detailed tasting record stands out, so read the cup as you would other Mengku raw tea: expect thick leaf, sweetness and force, and start with short steeps.

Old gardens here are limited, and near Banggai Dazhai only stumps of old trees remain at one old garden site. Treat old-tree claims with care and ask where the trees stand.
history:
Banggai had old gardens before the modern planting wave. Between 1958 and 1980 a large area of new gardens went in around here and neighbouring Bingshan, with seed brought from Bingdao, Gongnong and Banggai itself.

The main Lahu village, Banggai Dazhai or Laozhai, has 99 households, the second-largest Lahu settlement on the western half-mountain after Xiaohusai.
